title: The software engineering profession
audience: a computer science graduate or an experienced self-taught programmer preparing for and starting a software engineering job
purpose: Thrive as a working engineer: how software teams and companies work, the roles on a team, technical writing, communication, estimating and managing your own work, working in large codebases, on-call duty, incidents and blameless postmortems, open source and licenses, ethics and professional responsibility, accessibility, privacy and inclusive design, career paths, and continuous learning and mentoring.
primary_reading: ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct

weeks.1: How software teams and companies work
weeks.2: Roles: engineers, product managers, designers and others
weeks.3: Technical writing: design documents and READMEs
weeks.4: Communication: status updates, meetings and asking for help
weeks.5: Estimating and managing your own work
weeks.6: Working in legacy code and large codebases
weeks.7: On-call duty, incidents and blameless postmortems
weeks.11: Career paths: levels, specialties and growth

blocks.deliverable: Map the roles and decisions in a supplied project.
Estimate a supplied feature and track it.
Week 7 midterm; write a postmortem for a supplied incident.
Analyze an ethics case with the ACM Code.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Professional portfolio: a design document, a postmortem, an ethics case analysis, a plan for contributing to an open-source project, and a one-year career growth plan, each written to the standard a senior engineer would expect.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
